content: For medical advice regarding side effects, consult your doctor. In Canada, contact your doctor for guidance on side effects. Precautions: Before using etonogestrel, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other progestins (e.g., norethindrone, desogestrel), to any anesthetics or antiseptics that may be used during the procedure, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may cause dizziness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are certain you can perform them safely. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. This medication may lead to blotchy, dark areas on your face and skin (melasma). Sunlight can intensify this effect. Minimize your exposure to sunlight, and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. This product must not be used during pregnancy. If you become pregnant or suspect you might be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. This medication can pass into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain drugs may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), ritonavir, and St. John’s Wort. Inform your doctor when starting any new medication and discuss whether you should use reliable backup birth control. This medication may interfere with specific laboratory tests (e.g., sex-hormone-binding globulin, thyroid tests), potentially causing inaccurate results. Overdose: If this implant is swallowed, it may be harmful. If someone has ingested it and is experiencing severe symptoms such as fainting or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Notes: While using this medication, regular comprehensive physical exams, including laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., blood pressure, breast exams, pelvic exams, Pap smears), should be conducted. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. Storage: Not applicable. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
